```{r data preprocessing}
library(disdat)
library(mgcv)
library(sf)
library(spatstat)
library(fields)
library(tmap)
library(grid)
library(units)
set.seed(0)

#Preprocessing data
all = disData("NSW")
po = disPo("NSW")
bg = disBg("NSW")

head(po)
names(po)
unique(po$spid)

species_counts = table(po$spid)
species = names(which.max(species_counts))
species
species_counts[species]

po_sp = po[po$spid == species, ]

setdiff(names(po_sp), names(bg))

#po_sp$lon = po_sp$x
#po_sp$lat = po_sp$y

#project border
library(units)
border_lonlat = disBorder("NSW")

#project presence points
po_sp_lonlat = st_as_sf(po_sp, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) #convert to sf object, remove = FALSE keeps x, y
bg_lonlat = st_as_sf(bg, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

target_crs = 3577 # Australian Albers, coordinates in metres

border_proj = st_transform(border_lonlat, crs = target_crs) #convert coordinates
po_sp_proj = st_transform(po_sp_lonlat, crs = target_crs) 
bg_proj = st_transform(bg_lonlat, crs = target_crs)

coords_po = st_coordinates(po_sp_proj) #retrieve coordinates in matrix form
coords_bg = st_coordinates(bg_proj)

po_model = st_drop_geometry(po_sp_proj)
bg_model = st_drop_geometry(bg_proj)

po_model$x = coords_po[, "X"]/1000 # kilometres
po_model$y = coords_po[, "Y"]/1000

bg_model$x <- coords_bg[, "X"]/1000
bg_model$y <- coords_bg[, "Y"]/1000

save(po_model, file = "po_model.RDATA")
save(bg_model, file = "bg_model.RDATA")

#check points and boundary
map_po <- tm_shape(border_proj) + # create tmap object
  tm_polygons() + # add the border
  tm_shape(po_sp_proj) + # create tmap object for the points to overlay
  tm_dots(size = 0.2, col = "blue", alpha = 0.6, legend.show = FALSE) + # add the points
  tm_compass(type = "8star", position = c("left", "top")) + # add north arrow
  tm_layout(main.title = "Training data", main.title.position = "center") + # manage the layout
  tm_grid(lwd = 0.2, labels.inside.frame = FALSE, alpha = 0.4, crs = 4326, # add the grid
          labels.format = list(big.mark = ",", fun = function(x){paste0(x, "º")})) # add degree symbol

  graphics.off()          # close corrupted/open graphics devices
  tmap_mode("plot")       # ensure static plotting mode
  print(map_po)

covar_names = c("cti", "disturb", "mi", "rainann", "raindq", "rugged",
                "soildepth", "soilfert", "solrad", "tempann", "tempmin", "topo", "vegsys")

po_keep = complete.cases(po_model[, covar_names])
bg_keep = complete.cases(bg_model[, covar_names])

po_sp_lonlat = po_sp_lonlat[po_keep, ]
bg_lonlat = bg_lonlat[bg_keep, ]

domain_area_km2 <- as.numeric(set_units(sum(st_area(border_proj)), km^2))

#win = as.owin(border_sf) #st_sfc holds list of geometry objects --> observation window, NA_crs_ strip coordinate reference system
```


```{r gam}
quad_wt <- domain_area_km2 / nrow(bg_model) #quadrature weights

#processed dataframes
presence_df = data.frame(
  x = po_model$x, y = po_model$y,
  po_model[, covar_names],
  pt = 1, 
  wt = 1e-6)

quad = data.frame(
  x = bg_model$x, y = bg_model$y,
  bg_model[, covar_names],
  pt = 0,
  wt = quad_wt)

#combine presence and quadrature points
dat = rbind(presence_df, quad) 

dat$vegsys <- factor(dat$vegsys)

#scale
cont_vars <- setdiff(covar_names, "vegsys")
dat_scaled = scale(dat[, cont_vars])
centers = attr(dat_scaled, "scaled:center")
scales  = attr(dat_scaled, "scaled:scale")
dat[, cont_vars] = as.data.frame(dat_scaled) 

bg_covariates_raw = bg_model[, cont_vars, drop = FALSE] # preserves dimensions - dataframe/matrix

#inhomogeneous Poisson process
f1 <- pt / wt ~ tempann + rainann + rugged
ipp <- glm(f1, data = dat, family = poisson,  weights = wt)
coef(ipp)

#spatial range parameter - optimising with respect to rho, optimise REML criterion that penalises roughness - optimise marginal L (marginalising over b_j and approximated via Laplace)
presence_xy = as.matrix(presence_df[, c("x", "y")])

dists <- nndist(presence_xy) #nearest neigh dist.
range_interval <- range(dists[dists != 0])
range_interval <- quantile(dists, probs = c(0.1, 0.9), na.rm = TRUE)

objective_fn = function(rho) {
  tmp.m = gam(pt / wt ~ tempann + rainann + rugged + s(x, y, bs = "gp", k = 100, m = c(3,rho)), #Gauss. Proce, m = (corr fn -- matern, range)
              data=dat, family=poisson(), weights=wt, method="REML")
  return(tmp.m$gcv.ubre) # the "method" specific criterion
}

load("opt.RDATA")
#opt <- optimize(objective_fn, interval = range_interval)
#save(opt, file = "opt.RDATA")

#log-Gaussian Cox process
f2 <- update(f1, ~. +  s(x, y, bs = "gp", k = 5, m = c(3, opt$minimum)))
m <- gam(f2, data = dat, family = poisson(),  weights = wt, method = "REML")

# create grid 
grid_cells_proj = st_make_grid(
  border_proj,
  n = c(200, 200),
  what = "polygons"
)
grid_centres_proj <- st_centroid(grid_cells_proj)

# keep cells with centres that lie within border of NSW
inside <- lengths(st_within(grid_centres_proj, border_proj)) > 0 # st_within checks if spatial features are completely inside other features
grid_cells_proj <- grid_cells_proj[inside]
save(grid_cells_proj, file = "grid_cells_proj.RDATA")

grid_centres_proj <- grid_centres_proj[inside]

# extract coordinates 
grid_coords_m = st_coordinates(grid_centres_proj)

grid_xy <- data.frame(
  x = grid_coords_m[, "X"]/1000,
  y = grid_coords_m[, "Y"]/1000
)

# Using unscaled background covariates as response in thin plate spline
cont_vars_new = c("tempann", "rainann", "rugged")

load("grid_xy.RDATA")
library(fields)
#for (cn in cont_vars_new) {
#  fit_cov = Tps(x = cbind(bg_model$x, bg_model$y), Y = bg_covariates_raw[[cn]]) #thin plate spline regression - fits smooth multidim surface to irregularly spaced data
#  raw_pred = as.numeric(predict(fit_cov, as.matrix(grid_xy[, c("x", "y")])))
#  grid_xy[[cn]] = (raw_pred - centers[[cn]]) / scales[[cn]] # apply dat's scaling
#}

#save(grid_xy, file = "grid_xy.RDATA")

#predict the fitted intensity at every grid cell
grid_xy$z = predict(m, newdata = grid_xy, type = "response")

grid_pred_proj = st_sf(intensity = grid_xy$z,
                       log_intensity = log(grid_xy$z),
                       geometry = grid_cells_proj) #simple feature obj, dataframe containing spatial geometries
grid_pred_lonlat = st_transform(grid_pred_proj, target = 4326)

# Mapping according to vignette
intensity_map = function(grid_pred_lonlat, title){
  map <- tm_shape(border_lonlat) + # create tmap object
    tm_polygons() + # add border
    tm_shape(grid_pred_lonlat) + # create tmap object for points to overlay
    tm_polygons(fill = "log_intensity",
                fill.scale = tm_scale_continuous(
                  values = "turbo",
                  limits =  c(-8, 0),
                  outliers.trunc = c(TRUE, TRUE)),
                col = NA,
                fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Log fitted intensity")) +
    tm_shape(po_sp_lonlat) +
    tm_dots(size = 0.2, fill = "red", shape = 4, fill_alpha = 0.8) + #, fill.legend = tm_legend_hide()) + # add the points
    tm_compass(type = "8star", position = c("left", "top")) + # add north arrow
    tm_title(title) + # manage the layout
    tm_grid(lwd = 0.2, labels.inside.frame = FALSE, alpha = 0.4, crs = 4326, # add the grid
            labels.format = list(big.mark = ",", fun = function(x){paste0(x, "º")})) # add degree symbol
  
#  graphics.off()          # close corrupted/open graphics devices
#  tmap_mode("plot")       # ensure static plotting mode
#  print(map)
  
#  tmap_arrange(
#    map_po,
#    map,
#    ncol = 2)
}
save(intensity_map, file = "intensity_map.RDATA")
gam_map = intensity_map(grid_pred_lonlat, title = "gam")
save(gam_map, file = "gam_map.RDATA")
print(gam_map)

# calculate the observed, simulated K functions -- distinguishes true small-scale clustering or inhibition from environmental gradients.
border_km = st_union(st_geometry(border_proj))/1000
st_crs(border_km) = NA
win = as.owin(st_sf(geometry = border_km))

po_sp_ppp = ppp(x = presence_df$x,
                y = presence_df$y,
                window = win)
save(po_sp_ppp, file = "po_sp_ppp.RDATA")

plot(win)
points(po_sp_ppp, pch = 1, col = "red", size = 0.8)

# set the domain data points (quadrature used)
domain.grid <- subset(grid_xy, select = -z)

# predict intensity values
domain.grid$z = predict(m, newdata=domain.grid, type = "response")

# parameter values
smooth = predict(m, newdata = domain.grid, type = "terms", terms = "s(x,y)")
var_smooth = var(drop(smooth))
domain.grid$mu = predict(m, newdata = domain.grid, type = "link", exclude = "s(x,y)")
fixed.im = as.im(domain.grid[, c("x", "y", "mu")], W = win)
# create  pixel images
pred.im = as.im(domain.grid[,c("x","y","z")], W = win)

# simulate the envelopes/bounds
gam_K_obs <- Kinhom(po_sp_ppp, lambda = pred.im, correction = "border")
gam_K_env <- envelope(po_sp_ppp, fun = Kinhom, simulate = expression(rLGCP(model = "matern", mu = fixed.im, var = var_smooth, nu = 3/2, scale = sqrt(3)*opt$minimum)))

# Create Inhomogeneous K-func graphs
Kfunc = function(K_obs, K_env){
  plot(K_env$r, K_env$mmean, type = "n", ylim = range(c(K_env$obs, K_env$hi, K_env$lo)), ylab = "", xlab = "") #r = seq. of distance at which K-func eval. mmean = mean K(r), range contains both observed func, complete sim. envelope hi & lo
  polygon(c(rev(K_env$r), K_env$r), c(rev(K_env$hi), K_env$lo), col = 'grey80', border = NA) #rev() to trace the outside of the envelope
  lines(K_env$r, K_env$mmean, lty = "dashed")
  lines(K_obs$r, K_obs$border, col = "red")
  mtext(text = "distance (km)", side = 1, srt = 90, cex = 1, line = 2)
  mtext(text = "Inhomogeneous K Function", side = 2, srt = 90, cex = 1, xpd = T, line = 2.5)
  mtext(text = "log-Gaussian Cox Process", side = 3, cex = 1, line = 0.5, adj = 0)
  legend("bottomright", legend = c("Observed", "Theoretic", "95% Sim. Bounds"),
         col = c("red", "black", "grey80"), lty = c("solid", "dashed", "solid"), cex = 0.7,
         lwd = c(2, 2, 2), bty = "n")
}
save(Kfunc, file = "Kfunc.RDATA")
gam_kfunc = Kfunc(gam_K_obs, gam_K_env)

mu = predict(m, newdata = dat, type = "response")

#weighted Poisson-process log-likelihood (DWPR/Berman-Turner approximation)
loglik_new = sum(dat$wt * (dat$pt * log(mu) - mu))
cat("loglik:", loglik_new)
```


```{r scampr}
presence_df = data.frame(
  x = po_model$x, y = po_model$y,
  po_model[, covar_names],
  presence = 1, 
  quad.size = 0) #quadrature weights not used at the point events

quad = data.frame(
  x = bg_model$x, y = bg_model$y,
  bg_model[, covar_names],
  presence = 0,
  quad.size = quad_wt)

dat = rbind(presence_df, quad) 

dat$vegsys <- factor(dat$vegsys)

#scale
dat_scaled = scale(dat[, cont_vars])
centers = attr(dat_scaled, "scaled:center")
scales  = attr(dat_scaled, "scaled:scale")
dat[, cont_vars] = as.data.frame(dat_scaled) 
save(dat, file = "dat.RDATA")

bg_covariates_raw = bg_model[, cont_vars, drop = FALSE] # preserves dimensions - dataframe/matrix

#####################################
## Fit an IPP and LGCP to the data ##
#####################################

# using scampr():

# fit an IPP
library(scampr)
m.ipp <- scampr(presence ~ tempann + rainann + rugged,
                data = dat, #predictors, coordinates, quadrature weights at point events and quadrature points
                coord.names = c("x", "y"), 
                quad.weights.name = "quad.size", # column name of quadrature weights in dat_po
                model.type = "PO",
                include.sre	= FALSE)

# fit an LGCP
m.lgcp_va <- scampr(presence ~ tempann + rainann + rugged,
                    data = dat,
                    coord.names = c("x", "y"),
                    quad.weights.name = "quad.size",
                    model.type = "PO",
                    include.sre	= TRUE,
                    sre.approx = "variational", # use either "variational" or "laplace" approximation
                    basis.functions = simple_basis(9, dat)) # additionally supply basis functions

# can fit increasingly dense, regular grids of basis functions
bf.search.res <- basis.search(m.ipp, # base model, usually an IPP
                              max.basis.functions = 300, # stopping point to configurations to trial
                              which.approx = "variational", return.model = FALSE) # LGCP model type: variational or Laplace (the latter longer to compute)
# use basis configuration that achieves maximum fitted likelihood
bfs <- simple_basis(bf.search.res$nodes[which.max(bf.search.res$ll)], dat)
# fit Laplace version of proposed model using "best" basis configuration:
m.lgcp_lp <- scampr(presence ~ tempann + rainann + rugged,
                    data = dat, model.type = "PO",
                    include.sre	= TRUE,
                    sre.approx = "laplace",
                    basis.functions = bfs)
save(m.lgcp_lp, file = "m.lgcp_lp.RDATA")

#predict the fitted intensity at every grid cell
grid_xy$z = predict(m.lgcp_lp, newdata = grid_xy, type = "response")

grid_pred_proj = st_sf(intensity = grid_xy$z,
                       log_intensity = log(grid_xy$z),
                       geometry = grid_cells_proj) #simple feature obj, dataframe containing spatial geometries
grid_pred_lonlat = st_transform(grid_pred_proj, target = 4326)

# Mapping according to vignette
scampr_map = intensity_map(grid_pred_lonlat, title = "scampr")
save(scampr_map, file = "scampr_map.RDATA")
print(scampr_map)

#ERROR
#kinhom_lgcp <- kfunc_envelopes(m.lgcp_lp, # LGCP model
#                               nsims = 1000, # change to 1000 to replicate results presented in paper
#                               return.data = T)

# Calculate the observed, simulated K functions
domain.grid = subset(grid_xy, select = -z)
# predict intensity values
domain.grid$z = predict(m.lgcp_lp, newdata=domain.grid, type = "response")

# parameter values
var_u = m.lgcp_lp$prior.variances[, "Estimate"]
vars <- rep(var_u, m.lgcp_lp$basis.per.res)
Z_grid = as.matrix(get.bf.matrix(m.lgcp_lp, grid_xy[, c("x", "y")], bf.matrix.type = "sparse"))
var_smooth_grid <- drop(Z_grid^2 %*% vars)
var_smooth = mean(var_smooth_grid)
domain.grid$mu = predict(m.lgcp_lp, newdata = domain.grid, type = "link", dens = "prior")
fixed.im = as.im(domain.grid[, c("x", "y", "mu")], W = win)
# create  pixel images
pred.im = as.im(domain.grid[,c("x","y","z")], W = win)

# simulate the envelopes/bounds
scampr_K_obs <- Kinhom(po_sp_ppp, lambda = pred.im, correction = "border") #marginal.im
scampr_K_env <- envelope(po_sp_ppp, fun = Kinhom, simulate = expression(rLGCP(model = "matern", mu = fixed.im, var = var_smooth, nu = 3/2, scale = m.lgcp_lp$basis.fn.info$scale[1]))) #sqrt(3)*opt$minimum

# Create Inhomogeneous K-func graphs
scampr_kfunc = Kfunc(scampr_K_obs, scampr_K_env)

mu = predict(m, newdata = dat, type = "response")

#weighted Poisson-process log-likelihood (DWPR/Berman-Turner approximation)
loglik_new = sum(dat$wt * (dat$pt * log(mu) - mu))
cat("loglik:", loglik_new)
```
